corrected_fields.summary: The Basel Framework is the comprehensive compilation of all standards set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), the primary global standard setter for prudential bank regulation. This 1982-page PDF document covers capital definitions, risk-based capital requirements, credit risk approaches, market risk frameworks, operational risk, leverage ratios, and other prudential standards that internationally active banks must implement. Note: The specific publication date of this framework version is not stated in the document.
corrected_fields.why_it_matters: This is the foundational regulatory reference for global bank capital and risk standards. While not a specific policy announcement, it defines the rules that govern bank capital requirements, risk weighting methodologies, and market risk calculations—all of which affect how banks allocate capital and the cost of market-making activities.
corrected_fields.macro_context: The Basel Framework provides the regulatory architecture that shapes bank behavior globally. Key sections cover: banking book vs trading book boundaries; standardised and internal models approaches for market risk; counterparty credit risk frameworks; and capital treatment for securities financing transactions.
